elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added clause states that Vendor “shall defend” Customer from covered third-party claims.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added clause states that Vendor “shall…indemnify” Customer from covered third-party claims and resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates must receive the Vendor defence and indemnity protection.
elements.evidence: The beneficiaries are expressly “Customer and its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity obligations must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added obligation expressly applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity must cover allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) covers an allegation that the “Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) covers “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data “caused by Vendor,” which operatively covers a Vendor-caused data breach.

elements.element: Vendor's defence and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) expressly covers “Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The procedure requires the indemnified Party to give “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnifying party must control the defence of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The procedure states that “the indemnifying Party shall control the defence of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation in the defence.
elements.evidence: The procedure requires the indemnified Party to “provide reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers third-party claims arising from “Customer-provided content.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers third-party claims arising from “Customer's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The former indemnity for every claim relating to Customer's use is replaced with an indemnity limited to third-party claims arising from the two specified grounds, with no additional Customer indemnity trigger stated.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The added clause provides Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Customer appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include an option for Vendor to procure continued rights to use the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No operative procurement remedy is included. Section 9.3 merely references remedies allegedly required by Section 20.5 and does not itself create such a remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include an option for Vendor to modify the affected Services or Deliverables to become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No operative modification remedy appears in the rendered language; the unsupported Section 20.5 reference is insufficient.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include an option for Vendor to replace the affected Services or Deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: No operative replacement remedy appears in the rendered language; the unsupported Section 20.5 reference is insufficient.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include a refund remedy if the affected Services or Deliverables cannot be procured, modified, or replaced.
elements.evidence: No operative refund remedy appears in the rendered language; the unsupported Section 20.5 reference is insufficient.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap rather than being unlimited or subject only to an ordinary cap.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no liability cap applicable to Vendor's indemnity.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity super-cap must equal three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No three-times-annual-fees cap is stated.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position: it adds the required Vendor defence and indemnity triggers and beneficiaries, includes notice/control/cooperation procedures, and narrows Customer's indemnity to the two permitted grounds. Because the preferred level is complete, omission of the fallback's Vendor-favorable exclusions and cap does not defeat the preferred position. The fallback is independently unsatisfied because its exclusions, four-part IP remedy structure, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The drafting is generally clear and targeted, although the continuing reference to remedies required by Section 20.5 is unsupported by any provided operative Section 20.5 language.
